catalog_quote: In terms of word prosody, Sgaw Karen does not exhibit word stress cues, but does maintain a prosodic distinction between the more prominent major syllable and the phonologically reduced minor syllable. [p. ii] ... In short, contrary to the stress correlates found in some tonal languages, intensity and duration in Sgaw Karen are not found to correlate to syllable position consistently. Moreover, duration and intensity patterns do not seem linked to the age or sex of the speaker. This section has presented the finding that neither intensity nor duration consistently distinguish major syllables within a word, suggesting that word-level stress is not a feature of Sgaw Karen. [p. 24] ... Although there is no consistent marking of stress between major syllables, a reduced status of minor syllables and strong status of word-final position is supported by word-shape distribution (§3.3), reducti…

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: every segment of the deciding quotation, and the srule fragments, are verbatim in the held West 2017 text at the stated pages (ii, 24, 32-33); Gilmore 1898 sec. 14-15 (six tones) also held. (2) The classification 'no-word-stress' (strict=false) rests on a 2017 instrumental MA thesis whose explicit research question is Sgaw word stress, supervised by Sun-Ah Jun; among Glottolog's 25 descriptive refs the grammars are 1842-1961 missionary/structuralist works and the phonologies are Puttachart 1983 (124 pp MA), Sarvestani 2018 (183 pp PhD) and Fischer 2013 (sketch). None of these is known to contain a stress experiment; West's own literature review says prior descriptions have 'little to no description of word prosody'.
